title_zh: 连环画《西游记02：龙宫借宝》
title_en: Comic Book 'Journey to the West 02: Borrowing Treasures from the Dragon Palace'
source_file: 连环画《西游记02：龙宫借宝》（6-10岁）.pdf
full_text_zh:
[P1] 龙宫借宝
《西游记》之二
原著 吴承恩
改编 尚羡智
绘画 高同宝
河北美术出版社

[P2] 内容提要
《龙宫借宝》是《猴王出世》的续集。此集叙述孙悟空得道后，辞别了须菩提祖师，离了灵台方寸山斜月三星洞，回到花果山水帘洞，打跑了强占水帘洞府的混世魔王，重整洞府。
又从傲来国取来了各种刀枪器械，每日教众小猴操演武艺，怎奈他自己没有称手的兵刃和盔甲。经老猴提醒，孙悟空便到东海龙宫去借，经过好多周折，终于觅得凤翅紫金冠，锁子黄金甲，藕丝步云鞋和如意金箍棒。
1 自从悟空消灭了混世魔王，夺得了一口大刀以后，每日操练武艺。他教小猴们削竹为枪，削木为刀；分成两队，练习打仗。

[P3] 2 一天，悟空忽然静坐不语，像是思虑什么事情。四个老猴上前问道：‘大王思虑何事？’悟空道：‘我们这样练武，若叫玉帝知道，定说我们造反，他若派人捉拿，这竹枪、木刀怎能对付？’
3 大家一听悟空的话，都觉得有理，便问哪里有武器，悟空道：‘我也正为此事为难。’老猴们想了想说：‘这却不难，从这里往东走，有一傲来国，那里制造兵器，买些来也就是了。’

[P4] 4 悟空一听，心中大喜，又问：‘有多少路程？’老猴道：‘二百里水路。’悟空把家中之事略做安排，便登上云头到傲来国去置买兵器。
5 悟空一个跟斗，跃出二百里水路。他在高空往下一看，只见人们来来往往，很像赶集的一般。悟空心想：这一定是傲来国，待我下去一看。

[P5] 6 他落到地上，果然看见一座城市，里边六街三市，万户千门，行人车马来往不断。悟空想：这里定有现成兵器，我若去买，还不如使个神通弄他些来为妙。
7 他念起诀咒，吸了一大口气，然后吹了出去。马上狂风四起，飞沙走石，只慌得人们东逃西散，家家关门闭户。

[P6] 8 悟空转身来到兵器馆，只见刀、枪、剑、戟、斧、钺、钩、叉，长短兵器，样样俱备。他心中十分欢喜。
9 悟空刚要动手搬动，忽然又想：我一人能拿多少？不如使上个分身法。他随手拔下一撮毫毛，放进嘴里。

[P7] 10 他又把毫毛喷出口外，叫声“变！”毫毛马上变成千百个小猴。这些小猴见了兵器乱搬乱抢，力大的拿六七件，力小的拿三四件。
11 不大一会儿，兵器馆的兵器被搬得干干净净。悟空又驾起云风，带领众猴回花果山去了。

[P8] 12 悟空回到花果山，收了云雾，收了毫毛，将大小兵器堆在山前，说道：‘小的们，都来领兵器！’这时，正在操练的众猴，一见有了真刀真枪，又惊又喜。
13 猴子们像潮水一般跑上前去，争刀夺剑，抓斧取枪，一个个欢天喜地打闹起来。

[P9] 14 第二天，猴子们像往日一样，排列整齐，操练武艺。悟空站在高处，看着这四万五千多猴兵，手执明亮的武器，个个耀武扬威，精神百倍，心中十分高兴。
15 花果山这一练兵不大要紧，却惊动了邻山的怪兽和各路的妖王，他们见悟空武力强大，都来进金鼓，进彩旗，进盔甲。并拜悟空为王。

[P10] 16 一天，猴们正在操练，悟空将手中大刀扔在地上，说道：‘你们都有件称心的武器，我呢？就这口刀，轻如鸡毛，实在不称我的心！’
17 老猴们见悟空烦恼，便上前说道：‘大王乃仙圣，这口刀当然不能称心如意。但不知大王是否能入水里？’悟空道：‘自得道之后，能七十二变，上天有路，入地有门，水不淹，火不伤……当然能入水里。’

[P11] 18 老猴们笑嘻嘻说道：‘大王既有如此神通，自然能万事如愿。自古道：‘要得宝，龙宫找。’我们这铁板桥下，可通东海龙宫，你可找老龙王去借武器。’悟空听罢，高兴地说：‘好，待我试来。’
19 悟空跳到桥头，用分水法分开水路，钻进水里。

[P12] 20 悟空见前面闪闪发光，推想定是水晶宫，他便直奔前去。
21 正走时，忽然一夜叉又拦住道：“哪边来的？是何神圣？说明之后，也好通报迎接。”悟空道：“我乃花果山大圣孙悟空，是你家龙王的近邻，怎不相认？”

[P13] 22 夜叉听罢，赶忙进宫通报道：‘禀奏大王，外面有个花果山的大圣孙悟空，口称大王近邻，要见大王。’
23 龙王一听，忙带领龙子龙孙，虾兵蟹将出宫迎接。

[P14] 24 龙王把悟空迎进宫中，问道：‘上仙几时得道？有何仙术？’悟空道：‘我自得道，练得不死不灭。近因练武守护山洞，缺少一件称心的武器，特来仙宫借宝。’
25 龙王一听此情不好推脱，便命鳜都司取出一把长杆大刀。悟空摇摇头说：‘俺老孙不会使刀，请另借一件。’

[P15] 26 龙王又命鲌大尉领鳝力士取出一根九股叉。悟空接过来，耍了一阵，放下说：‘轻！轻！轻！叉不可手，请再换一件。’
27 龙王心中有些恐惧，便又命水卒抬过一杆方天化戟。这戟足有七千二百斤重。

[P16] 28 悟空上前，用手掂一掂，笑道：‘还是太轻！’龙王越发害怕，说道：‘上仙，我宫中只有这件武器最重，再没别的兵器了。’
29 龙王正在为难，龙女、龙婆上前说道：‘大王，观看此圣决非寻常。那块神珍铁近日霞光艳艳，莫非此仙应得？’龙王道：‘那是大禹治水镇压江河的铁柱，怎能当得武器？’

[P17] 30 悟空一听神铁，便对龙王说道：“神铁也好，拿来我看。”龙王道：“那是一块神珍铁，拿不起，背不动。上仙若是喜爱，可亲自去看。”说罢，二人便到海底宝库去观看神铁。
31 进了宝库，只见霞光艳艳，瑞气腾腾，龙王道：“上仙请看，那放光的便是。”悟空上前一摸，原来是一根铁柱，大约有斗来粗细，二丈多长。

[P18] 32 悟空用力摇了摇，左看看，右看看，然后说道：“好却好，就是太粗太长，若能短些、细些才好。”说也奇怪，悟空话音刚落，那宝贝便细了一圈，短了几尺。
33 悟空叫它再细、再短，果然又细了几圈，短了几尺。他拿在手里一看，原来两头包有金箍，中间是一段黑铁，上写：如意金箍棒，重一万三千五百斤。

[P19] 34 悟空拿了金箍棒，高兴地说道：“此宝为何埋藏龙宫多年，今日才发出光亮？噢！想必该我悟空所得；这真是宝贝如人意。”
35 悟空抡起金箍棒，来到水晶宫。只吓得老龙王胆战心惊，小龙王魂飞魄散，鱼、鳖、虾、蟹一个个战战兢兢。

[P20] 36 悟空把宝贝拿在手中，坐在水晶宫殿上，对龙王笑道：“多谢厚意。”龙王道：“不敢，不敢。”悟空道：“虽有武器，却还少一身盔甲，烦贤邻帮忙借用一副。
37 龙王推却道：“这里实在没有了，到别家借吧！”悟空道：“一客不烦二主，走三家不如坐一家。”龙王道：“真的没有了。”悟空把金箍棒一抡道：“可晓得此铁！”

[P21] 38 老龙王哪敢不应，他忙派龟将、鳖帅敲响金钟，擂响铁鼓，邀请南海、北海、西海的龙王前来商量。
39 不一会儿，南海龙王敖钦、北海龙王敖顺、西海龙王敖闰，一齐来到老龙王这里。

[P22] 40 老龙王迎出来，悄悄地把悟空借宝之事告诉了他们。
41 南海龙王一听，便大怒道：“不必客气，咱们点动兵将，捉住他便了。”老龙王摆摆手道：“使不得，使不得！他有根一万多斤重的铁棒，只要碰着，性命难保。”

[P23] 42 西海龙王思虑了一会儿，便对大家说道：‘我有一妙计：可先给他盔甲，打发他出去，然后报知玉帝，再派兵追拿。’大家都点头称赞这一主张。
43 这几个龙王有的拿出藕丝步云鞋，有的拿出锁子黄金甲，有的拿出凤翅紫金冠。老龙王一见心中大喜，便领他们走进宫殿。

[P24] 44 悟空将拿出来的衣冠穿戴整齐，便对龙王道：“打扰了！”说完，舞起金箍棒，打出水晶宫去。
45 四个龙王只气得怒满胸膛，他们连忙商量着给玉帝写奏本，请求派天兵天将捉拿悟空。

[P25] 46 悟空手提金箍棒，分开水道，回到铁板桥头。迎接他的猴兵见他全身明光光，金灿灿，便一齐喝彩迎接。
47 悟空满面春风，高登宝座，将金箍棒竖在当中。众猴上前又摸又看，但是谁也拿不起来，一个个咬指伸舌道：
“爷爷，这样重，你怎能拿得动？”

[P26] 48 悟空把金箍棒的来历说了一遍，然后将铁棒提在手中叫道：“小！小！小！”马上金箍棒小成绣花针一般。
49 悟空又将金箍棒竖起，叫声：“大！大！大！”金箍棒又变成斗来粗细，二丈长短。

[P27] 50 悟空走出洞来，抡舞了一会儿金箍棒，便躬身道：
“长！”这时，他长的有万丈多高，只见他头如泰山，腰如
峻岭，眼如闪电。手中的金箍棒上到三十三天，下到十八
层地狱。
51 这一来不大要紧，却惊动了满山的虎、豹、狼、蛇
和七十二洞的怪兽，他们都赶来拜见悟空，称赞悟空的本
领。

[P28] 52 后来又与牛魔王、蛇魔王、鹏魔王、狮驼王、猕猴王、禺狨王结拜为兄弟。他们每日游海玩山，讲文论武。
53 花果山飘起一面大旗，猴兵插起大鼓，震天动地。悟空站在高山之上，和众兄弟观看猴兵操练武艺，那猴兵一个个齐整健壮，威风凛凛精神百倍。

[P29] 54 从此，悟空便名扬四海了。他凭这得力的武器走南闯北，大闹天宫。又保唐僧西天取经，做了好多不凡之事。欲知详情，请看第三册《齐天大圣》。

full_text_en:
[P1] Dragon Palace Borrowing Treasures
Part Two of Journey to the West
Original work by Wu Cheng'en
Adapted by Shang Xianzhi
Illustrated by Gao Tongbao
Hebei Fine Arts Publishing House

[P2] Content Summary
"Dragon Palace Borrowing Treasures" is the sequel to "The Birth of the Monkey King." This volume narrates how, after attaining enlightenment, Sun Wukong bid farewell to his master, Master Subodhi, left the Sloping Moon Three Stars Cave on Lingtai Fangcun Mountain, returned to the Water Curtain Cave on Flower-Fruit Mountain, defeated the tyrant who had seized the cave, and restored his kingdom.
He then retrieved various weapons and armor from Aolai Kingdom, teaching the young monkeys martial arts every day. However, he himself lacked a suitable weapon and armor. After being reminded by an old monkey, Sun Wukong went to the Dragon Palace in the Eastern Sea to borrow them. After many difficulties, he finally obtained the Phoenix-Wing Golden Crown, the Chainmail Golden Armor, the Lotus-Thread Cloud-Shoes, and the如意 Golden Cudgel.
1 Since Wukong defeated the tyrant and obtained a large sword, he has been practicing martial arts every day. He taught the young monkeys to make spears from bamboo and swords from wood, dividing them into two teams to practice fighting.

[P3] 2 One day, Wukong suddenly sat quietly, as if pondering something. Four old monkeys approached and asked, 'Your Majesty, what are you thinking about?' Wukong replied, 'We practice martial arts like this. If the Jade Emperor finds out, he will surely say we are rebelling. If he sends people to capture us, how can we defend ourselves with bamboo spears and wooden swords?'
3 Upon hearing Wukong's words, everyone agreed. They asked where weapons could be found. Wukong said, 'I am also troubled by this matter.' The old monkeys thought for a moment and said, 'This is not difficult. Go east from here, and there is a country called Ailai. They make weapons there; we can just buy some.'

[P4] 4 Wukong, upon hearing this, was overjoyed and asked, 'How far is it?' The old monkey replied, 'Two hundred li by water.' Wukong made some arrangements at home, then mounted the clouds to go to Aolai Kingdom to buy weapons.
5 Wukong flipped one somersault, covering two hundred li of water. Looking down from the sky, he saw people coming and going, just like a busy market. Wukong thought to himself: This must be Aolai Kingdom. Let me go down and take a look.

[P5] 6 He landed on the ground and indeed saw a city, with six streets and three markets, ten thousand households and a thousand gates, with people and carriages coming and going constantly. Wukong thought: There must be ready-made weapons here; if I were to buy them, it would be better to use my supernatural powers to get some instead.
7 He recited a spell, took a big breath, and then blew it out. Immediately, a fierce wind arose, sand and stones flew, and people panicked, fleeing in all directions, while every household closed their doors and shutters.

[P6] 8 Wukong turned and arrived at the armory, where he saw swords, spears, blades, halberds, axes, battle-axes, hooks, and forks—long and short weapons, all fully equipped. He was very delighted.
9 Wukong was just about to move the weapons when he suddenly thought: How much can I carry by myself? I might as well use the body-splitting technique. He casually plucked a tuft of hair and put it in his mouth.

[P7] 10 He blew his body hairs out of his mouth and shouted, “Change!” The hairs instantly turned into hundreds of little monkeys. These little monkeys saw the weapons and started grabbing and carrying them wildly; the stronger ones took six or seven pieces, while the weaker ones took three or four.
11 In no time, all the weapons in the armory were carried away. Wukong then rode the cloud-wind again, leading the monkeys back to Flower-Fruit Mountain.

[P8] 12 Wukong returned to Flower-Fruit Mountain, gathered the clouds and mist, and collected his hairs, piling the weapons of various sizes at the foot of the mountain. He said, 'Come, little ones, come and take your weapons!' At that moment, the monkeys who were practicing martial arts, seeing real swords and spears, were both surprised and delighted.
13 The monkeys rushed forward like a tide, scrambling for swords and knives, grabbing axes and spears, each one joyfully playing and frolicking.

[P9] 14 The next day, the monkeys, as usual, stood in neat rows and practiced their martial arts. Wukong stood on a high place, watching the over forty-five thousand monkey soldiers, each holding bright weapons, showing off their might, full of spirit, and he felt extremely happy.
15 This military drill on Flower-Fruit Mountain, though not a big deal, startled the monsters from neighboring mountains and various demon kings. Seeing Wukong's great martial prowess, they all came to present golden drums, colorful banners, and helmets, and bowed to Wukong as their king.

[P10] 16 One day, while the monkeys were practicing, Wukong threw his large knife to the ground and said, 'You all have weapons that suit you, but me? This knife is as light as a chicken feather—it truly doesn't suit my heart!'
17 Seeing Wukong troubled, the old monkeys approached and said, 'Your Majesty is a sage. Of course this knife cannot satisfy you. But we wonder, can Your Majesty enter the water?' Wukong replied, 'Since I attained enlightenment, I can transform seventy-two times, find a path to heaven, enter the earth through a gate, remain unharmed by water or fire... of course I can enter the water.'

[P11] 18 The old monkeys laughed and said: 'Your Majesty, with such supernatural powers, you can surely achieve anything. As the old saying goes: 'To find treasure, go to the Dragon Palace.' Under our iron bridge, there is a passage to the Eastern Sea Dragon Palace. You should go ask the old Dragon King to lend you weapons.' Upon hearing this, Wukong happily replied: 'Alright, let me try.'
19 Wukong jumped to the bridgehead, used his water-parting technique to split the water, and dived into the sea.

[P12] 20 Wukong saw a shimmering light ahead and guessed it must be the Crystal Palace, so he rushed forward.
21 As he walked, suddenly a night guard blocked his path and asked, “Where are you from? Who are you? Please explain, so I can report and welcome you.” Wukong replied, “I am the Great Sage Sun Wukong from Flower-Fruit Mountain, a neighbor of your Dragon King. Why don’t you recognize me?”

[P13] 22 The night demon, upon hearing this, hurried into the palace to report: 'Your Majesty, there is a Great Sage Sun Wukong from Flower-Fruit Mountain outside, who claims to be your neighbor and wishes to see you.'
23 Upon hearing this, the Dragon King hurriedly led his dragon sons and grandsons, along with the shrimp soldiers and crab generals, out of the palace to welcome him.

[P14] 24 The Dragon King welcomed Wukong into the palace and asked, 'When did you attain immortality, noble immortal? What magical arts do you possess?' Wukong replied, 'I attained immortality myself and have trained to be deathless. Recently, I've been practicing martial arts to protect my mountain cave, but I lack a weapon that suits me. So I've come to borrow a treasure from your celestial palace.'
25 Upon hearing this, the Dragon King found it hard to refuse and ordered General Gui to bring out a long-handled great sword. Wukong shook his head and said, 'I, Old Sun, don't know how to use a sword. Please lend me something else.'

[P15] 26 The Dragon King then ordered General Bao and the eel warriors to bring out a nine-pronged spear. Wukong took it, twirled it around for a while, and put it down, saying: 'Light! Light! Light! This spear is not suitable for me. Please bring me another one.'
27 The Dragon King, feeling somewhat fearful, then ordered the water soldiers to bring forward a Fangtian Huajie. This halberd weighed as much as 7,200 jin.

[P16] 28 Wukong stepped forward, lifted the weapon with his hand, and laughed, 'Still too light!' The Dragon King grew increasingly frightened and said, 'Immortal, this is the heaviest weapon in my palace; we have no others.'
29 The Dragon King was at a loss. The Dragon Princess and Dragon Mother stepped forward and said, 'Your Majesty, this immortal is no ordinary being. That sacred iron has recently been glowing with radiant light—could it be meant for this immortal?' The Dragon King replied, 'That is the iron pillar used by Yu the Great to control the rivers and suppress the floods; how could it serve as a weapon?'

[P17] 30 Wukong, upon hearing about the divine iron, said to the Dragon King, "If it's divine iron, bring it to me to see." The Dragon King replied, "That is a divine treasure iron; it cannot be carried or moved. If the immortal likes it, you may go see it yourself." After saying this, the two went to the underwater treasure vault to view the divine iron.
31 Entering the treasure vault, they saw brilliant, radiant light and auspicious mist. The Dragon King said, "Immortal, please look—there is the glowing one." Wukong stepped forward and touched it, and found it was a large iron pillar, about as thick as a斗 (a measure) and over two zhang long.

[P18] 32 Wukong shook it hard, looked left and right, then said, “It’s good, but too thick and too long. If it could be shorter and thinner, that would be better.” Strange indeed—just as Wukong finished speaking, the treasure became thinner by a ring and shorter by several feet.
33 Wukong told it to become even thinner and shorter, and indeed, it became thinner by several rings and shorter by several feet. He took it in his hands and looked closely: the two ends were wrapped in golden rings, the middle was a black iron section, and it bore the inscription: ‘Ruyi Jingu Bang, weighing 13,500 jin.’

[P19] 34 Wukong took the Golden Cudgel and happily said, "Why has this treasure been buried in the Dragon Palace for so many years, only to shine brightly today? Ah! It must be meant for me, Wukong. This is truly a treasure that suits one's heart's desire."
35 Wukong swung the Golden Cudgel and arrived at the Crystal Palace. The old Dragon King was terrified, the young Dragon King was frightened to death, and the fish, turtles, shrimp, and crabs trembled with fear.

[P20] 36 Wukong held the treasure in his hand, sat on the crystal palace throne, and smiled at the Dragon King: "Thank you for your kindness." The Dragon King replied: "Not at all, not at all." Wukong said: "Although I now have a weapon, I still lack a suit of armor. I trouble you, my neighbor, to lend me one.
37 The Dragon King refused: "There really is nothing left here. Go borrow from someone else!" Wukong said: "One guest shouldn't trouble two hosts; visiting three homes is worse than staying in one." The Dragon King said: "There truly is nothing left." Wukong swung his Golden Cudgel and said: "Do you know what this iron is!"

[P21] 38 The old Dragon King dared not refuse. He hurriedly sent the turtle general and the crab commander to strike the golden bell and beat the iron drum, inviting the Dragon Kings of the South Sea, North Sea, and West Sea to come and discuss.
39 In no time, the Dragon King of the South Sea, Ao Qin, the Dragon King of the North Sea, Ao Shun, and the Dragon King of the West Sea, Ao Run, all arrived at the old Dragon King's place.

[P22] 40 The old Dragon King came out to greet them and quietly told them about Wukong borrowing the treasure.
41 Upon hearing this, the Dragon King of the South Sea became furious and said, “No need to be polite. Let’s mobilize our troops and capture him.” The old Dragon King waved his hand and said, “No, no! He has an iron staff weighing over ten thousand jin. If we touch it, we’ll lose our lives.”

[P23] 42 The Dragon King of the West Sea thought for a moment, then said to everyone: 'I have a clever plan: we can first give him armor, send him away, then report to the Jade Emperor and send troops to capture him.' Everyone nodded in approval of this suggestion.
43 These Dragon Kings took out lotus-silk cloud-walking shoes, some took out chainmail golden armor, and others took out phoenix-winged golden crowns. The old Dragon King, upon seeing this, was overjoyed and led them into the palace.

[P24] 44 Wukong put on the clothes and hats he had taken out, then said to the Dragon King, "Excuse me!" After that, he swung his Golden Cudgel and left the Crystal Palace.
45 The four Dragon Kings were furious with anger. They hurriedly discussed writing a memorial to the Jade Emperor, requesting that heavenly soldiers and generals be sent to capture Wukong.

[P25] 46 Wukong carried the Golden Cudgel, parted the waterway, and returned to the iron bridge. The monkey soldiers waiting for him saw that he was shining brightly and golden, and they all cheered and welcomed him.
47 Wukong, beaming with joy, ascended the throne and placed the Golden Cudgel upright in the center. The monkeys approached, touching and examining it, but none could lift it. One by one, they bit their fingers and stuck out their tongues, saying:
"Grandfather, it's so heavy—how can you possibly lift it?"

[P26] 48 Wukong explained the origin of the Golden Cudgel, then held the iron staff and shouted, “Small! Small! Small!” Immediately, the Golden Cudgel shrank to the size of a needle.
49 Wukong then raised the Golden Cudgel again and shouted, “Big! Big! Big!” The Golden Cudgel grew to the thickness of a bowl and about two zhang long.

[P27] 50 Wukong came out of the cave, twirled the Golden Cudgel for a while, then bowed and said: 
"Grow!" At that moment, he grew over ten thousand zhang tall. His head was like Mount Tai, his waist like a steep ridge, and his eyes like lightning. The Golden Cudgel in his hand reached up to the thirty-third heaven and down to the eighteenth layer of hell.
51 This was not a big deal, but it startled the tigers, leopards, wolves, snakes, and monsters from the seventy-two caves on the mountain. They all came to pay homage to Wukong and praised his skills.

[P28] 52 Later, he became sworn brothers with Niú Mó Wáng, Shé Mó Wáng, Péng Mó Wáng, Shī Tuó Wáng, Mí Hóu Wáng, and Yú Róng Wáng. They traveled the seas and mountains daily, discussing literature and martial arts.
53 A large banner flew over Huāguǒ Mountain, and the monkey soldiers raised great drums, shaking the heavens and earth. Wùkōng stood atop a high mountain, watching with his brothers as the monkey soldiers practiced their martial arts. The soldiers were neat, strong, and full of spirit, looking mighty and invincible.

[P29] 54 From then on, Wukong became famous throughout the four seas. With this powerful weapon, he traveled far and wide, causing chaos in Heaven, and later protected Tang Sanzang on his journey to the West to obtain scriptures, accomplishing many extraordinary deeds. For more details, please read the third volume, 'The Great Sage Equaling Heaven'.

full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本《龙宫借宝》的封面和扉页，标明该书为《西游记》之二，原著吴承恩，改编尚羡智，绘画高同宝，由河北美术出版社出版。
[P2] 本页为绘本《龙宫借宝》的内容提要，概述了孙悟空得道后回到花果山、击败混世魔王、重整洞府，并因缺乏称手兵器而前往东海龙宫借宝的故事情节。下方插图及文字描述了孙悟空教小猴们操练武艺的场景。
[P3] 孙悟空因担心练武被玉帝视为造反而忧虑，老猴们建议去东边的傲来国购买兵器。
[P4] 孙悟空得知傲来国距离花果山二百里水路后，安排好家中事务，驾云前往。途中他翻了一个跟斗，从高空俯瞰下方热闹的城镇，认定那就是傲来国，决定下去查看。
[P5] 孙悟空降落在傲来国，看到城市繁华，决定不买兵器而用神通夺取。他念咒吹气，引发狂风，使城中百姓惊慌逃散，家家关门闭户。
[P6] 孙悟空来到兵器馆，看到各种兵器齐全，十分欢喜；他准备搬运兵器时，想到一人拿不了多少，便决定使用分身法，拔下毫毛准备变出分身。
[P7] 孙悟空用毫毛变出众多小猴，分头将兵器馆的兵器搬空，随后带领众猴驾云返回花果山。
[P8] 孙悟空带着从傲来国夺取的兵器返回花果山，分发给众猴，猴子们欣喜若狂，争抢兵器，场面热闹非凡。
[P9] 第二天，孙悟空带领猴兵整齐操练武艺，场面壮观，他十分高兴；此举惊动了邻山怪兽和各路妖王，他们纷纷前来献礼，拜孙悟空为王。
[P10] 孙悟空在操练时嫌弃自己的刀太轻，老猴们见状询问他是否能入水，孙悟空自信地表示自己能七十二变，水火不侵，自然能入水。
[P11] 老猴们建议孙悟空去东海龙宫向龙王借兵器，孙悟空欣然同意，并跳入水中，用分水法潜入海底。
[P12] 孙悟空潜入东海，看见前方发光，认定是水晶宫便直奔而去，途中被一名夜叉拦住询问身份，孙悟空自称是花果山大圣，与龙王为邻。
[P13] 夜叉向龙王通报孙悟空来访，龙王随即带领龙子龙孙及虾兵蟹将出宫迎接。
[P14] 孙悟空被龙王迎进水晶宫，说明来意是借一件称心的兵器；龙王命鳜都司取出长杆大刀，但孙悟空表示不会用刀，要求另借一件兵器。
[P15] 孙悟空试用龙王提供的九股叉，觉得太轻不合用，要求再换一件；龙王心生畏惧，又命人抬出重达七千二百斤的方天化戟。
[P16] 孙悟空试用龙王提供的方天化戟，觉得太轻，龙王无奈表示已无更重兵器；龙女和龙婆建议将神珍铁（定海神针）赠予孙悟空，龙王则认为那是镇压江河的铁柱，不能当武器。
[P17] 孙悟空请求观看神珍铁，龙王带他前往海底宝库。在宝库中，孙悟空见到一根发光的铁柱，粗如斗、长二丈多。
[P18] 孙悟空在海底宝库中见到定海神针，试用后发现其能随心意变化粗细长短，最终确认其为如意金箍棒，重一万三千五百斤。
[P19] 孙悟空拿到金箍棒后欣喜若狂，认为此宝与自己有缘；随后他挥舞金箍棒回到水晶宫，令龙王和虾兵蟹将们惊恐万分。
[P20] 孙悟空得到金箍棒后，向龙王借盔甲，龙王推说没有，孙悟空便挥舞金箍棒威吓龙王。
[P21] 老龙王因孙悟空借走金箍棒而惊慌，派龟将和鳖帅敲钟击鼓，召集南海、北海、西海的龙王前来商议对策；不久后，三位龙王齐聚老龙王处。
[P22] 老龙王向南海、北海、西海龙王告知孙悟空借走宝物之事，南海龙王提议出兵捉拿，老龙王则因孙悟空持有重达万斤的铁棒而极力劝阻，担心性命难保。
[P23] 西海龙王提议先给孙悟空盔甲让他离开，再向玉帝报告派兵捉拿，其他龙王赞同此计；随后几位龙王拿出各自的宝物，老龙王大喜，带领他们进入宫殿。
[P24] 孙悟空穿戴好龙王提供的衣冠后，向龙王告别并挥舞金箍棒离开水晶宫；四位龙王气愤不已，商议向玉帝上奏，请求派天兵天将捉拿孙悟空。
[P25] 孙悟空手持金箍棒返回花果山，猴兵们欢呼迎接；他登座后将金箍棒竖立，众猴尝试搬动却无法举起，惊叹其重量。
[P26] 孙悟空向猴兵们讲述金箍棒的来历，并展示其能随口令变小或变大的神奇能力。
[P27] 孙悟空在花果山展示金箍棒的神通，命令其变长后身形巨大，惊动了满山的虎豹狼蛇和七十二洞的怪兽，它们纷纷前来拜见并称赞他的本领。
[P28] 孙悟空与牛魔王等六位魔王结拜为兄弟，每日游山玩水、讲文论武；随后在花果山竖起大旗、擂鼓，与兄弟们一同观看猴兵操练武艺，场面威武壮观。
[P29] 本页总结孙悟空获得金箍棒后名扬四海，并预告其后续大闹天宫、保护唐僧取经的传奇经历；同时附有《西游记》连环画的完整目录。
[P30] 本页为《龙宫借宝》连环画的版权页，列出了原著作者、改编者、绘者、出版发行信息、ISBN及定价等出版细节。
